chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a newborn, [whether] his head should be shaved after the seventh day, so he said: 'When seven days have passed, the shaving is not obligatory upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Is shaving a newborn's head obligatory after the seventh day in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the shaving of a newborn's head (*Aqiqah* ritual) is a recommended act (*Mustahabb*) rather than a strictly time-bound obligation (*Wajib*), as the specific window of the seventh day is not a rigid deadline for validity. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that while performing it on the seventh day is preferred to follow the Sunnah of the Prophet, delaying it does not incur sin or invalidate the act, emphasizing the flexibility in ritual gratitude.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the new-born, should one shave off his head after the seventh day?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the seven days pass by, so the shaving (of the head) is not upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the newborn: if shaving his head after seven days from his birth is required.
He (the Imam) said, ‘When seven days pass shaving is not required.’”
